body.statement: For every bounded nuisance candidate \(\eta=(s,u_0,u_1)\), including ties \(s=c\) assigned to the saturated branch, the exact identity is \[R(P,\eta)=\delta\mathbb E_P\!\left[\tau(X)|e(X)-c|\mathbf 1\!\left\{\mathbf 1\{s(X)<c\}\ne\mathbf 1\{e(X)<c\}\right\}\right]+\mathbb E_P\!\left[(s(X)-e(X))\left\{\mathbf 1\{s(X)<c\}\frac{(\delta-1)(u_0(X)-\mu_0(X))}{1-s(X)}+\mathbf 1\{s(X)\ge c\}\frac{u_1(X)-\mu_1(X)}{s(X)}\right\}\right].\] Every displayed denominator is bounded away from zero on its active branch. Consequently, if \(\|s-e\|_\infty\le\rho\), the branch-relevant outcome error is at most \(\varepsilon\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm m}(\alpha,C_{\mathrm m})\), then \(|R(P,\eta)|\le C_{\delta,M,C_{\mathrm m}}\{\rho\varepsilon+\rho^{1+\alpha}\}\).
body.justification: The equality isolates the only nonsmooth bias and gives the rate condition used by both frequentist one-step and posterior corrections.
body.gap: Kennedy's smooth stochastic-policy remainder has no crossing term, while Levis et al. give a margin upper envelope for different max-min bounds rather than this exact branch-specific identity.
body.consumer: Posterior and machine-learning users can verify root-\(n\) bias control using only the outcome regression on the branch that is actually observed with stable probability.
